Find the total surface area of the cylinder. Use the $\pi$ button on your calculator and give your answer correct to 1 decimal place, in $\text{cm}^{2}$.

canonical_solution.text_md: The $12\pi$ $\text{cm}$ side of the rectangle went once round the base, so it equals the circumference of the base circle: $2\pi r=12\pi$.
Divide both sides by $2\pi$ to find the radius of the circles: $r=6$ $\text{cm}$.
Area of the rectangle (the curved surface) $=(12\pi)\times(4)=48\pi$ $\text{cm}^{2}$.
Area of the two circular ends $=2\pi r^{2}=2\pi(6)^{2}=72\pi$ $\text{cm}^{2}$.
Surface area = rectangle + two circles $=48\pi+72\pi=120\pi\approx377.0$ $\text{cm}^{2}$.
